title: Native corruption remains fractured but not eradicated in this life
source_text: XVIII. Etenim quamdiu in hoc mortali corpore degimus, perpetuo manent in nobis pravitatis & corruptionis nativae reliquiae. Illa quidem eos qui sunt per veram atque vivam fidem Christo inserti amplius damnare non potest, & felicitate aeterna excludere: ac praeterea per Christi gratiam ita fracta & debilitata est, ut amplius in iis non regnet, sed spiritui cedat atque subjiciatur. Veruntamen non est penitus sublata & eradicata. Unde est quod fideles ipsi sentiunt se multum ad malum proclives, & in bene agendo difficultatem magnam experiuntur. Nec in iis ad mortem usque cessat, carnis adversus spiritum rebellio, quae legi divinae repugnat, illosque in diversum trahit, & contra quam ipsis perpetuo luctandum.
pass_a_gloss: For as long as we live in this mortal body, remains of native depravity and corruption perpetually remain in us. That indeed can no longer damn those who are inserted into Christ by true and living faith, nor exclude them from eternal happiness: and further by Christ's grace it is so fractured and weakened that it no longer reigns in them, but yields and is subjected to the Spirit. Nevertheless it is not utterly removed and eradicated. Hence it is that the faithful themselves feel themselves much inclined to evil, and experience great difficulty in doing well. Nor does the rebellion of flesh against spirit cease in them until death—rebellion which resists the divine law, pulls them contrary ways, and against which they must continually wrestle.
pass_b_english: Native corruption's remains stay in mortal life: fractured so they no longer reign or damn the grafted-in, yet not eradicated.
Believers feel strong evil-tilt and flesh-Spirit war until death.
